title: Your Cosmic Address
objective: After this level you can state Earth's address: third planet from the Sun, a star in the Milky Way.
summary: The Sun is a star, Earth is planet three, and our whole solar system lives in the Milky Way.

cards.headline: Every star you see at night is a sun. Ours is just the closest one.
cards.body: That little twinkle you wish on? It's a sun. It looks tiny for one reason only: it's unbelievably far away.

cards.headline: Your cosmic mailing address
cards.body: If aliens wanted to mail you a postcard, they'd need a long address. Line one: Earth. Line two: the third planet from the Sun, with two neighbors closer in and five farther out. Line three: the solar system, which is just the Sun plus everything swinging around it. And we're not done yet.

cards.fact: The Sun you see is 8 minutes old.
cards.context: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach us, so the Sun in the sky is the Sun from 8 minutes ago. If it vanished right now, you'd keep seeing it for about 8 more minutes. Light is the fastest thing there is. The Sun is just that far away.

mascot.line: Hold on to this 8-minute delay. Level 8 turns it into a whole way of measuring space.

cards.headline: Last line: the Milky Way
cards.body: The final line on the envelope is the Milky Way, a spiral of at least 100 billion stars. We live out in the suburbs, about 26,000 light-years from downtown. On a dark night, that hazy stripe across the sky is the rest of our galaxy. You're looking at your own neighborhood from the sidewalk.

cards.headline: Cosmic address: unlocked
learned: The Sun is a star, the closest one
Earth is the third of eight planets
Sunlight is about 8 minutes old when it arrives
Our solar system lives in the Milky Way

questions.prompt: Counting outward from the Sun, which planet is Earth?
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus, then Earth: third of the eight planets.

questions.prompt: Which is the most accurate description of the Sun?

options.label: One star among many in the Milky Way
The center of the Milky Way
options.rationale: The Sun orbits within the Milky Way; it isn't its center.

options.label: A planet that gives off light
options.rationale: Planets reflect light; the Sun is a star that makes its own.

options.label: The only star in our galaxy
options.rationale: The Milky Way has at least 100 billion stars.

questions.explanation: The Sun is an ordinary star, one of at least 100 billion in the Milky Way.

questions.prompt: Which list goes from smallest to largest?

options.label: Solar system → Earth → Milky Way
options.rationale: Earth is one part of the solar system.

options.label: Earth → Milky Way → solar system
options.rationale: The solar system sits inside the Milky Way.

questions.explanation: Earth is one planet in the solar system, and the whole solar system is one tiny part of the Milky Way.
